title: 122. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Converting Mass and Time Units
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a mass given in kilograms to grams correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(3\text{ kg}\) to \(\text{g}\).
questions.explanation: Use the source-to-target unit conversion: \(3\times 1{,}000=3{,}000\text{ g}\). The alternative \(300\text{ g}\) uses \(100\) grams per kilogram instead of \(1{,}000\).
questions.hint: Identify the source and target units before choosing a scale factor.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a mass given in grams to kilograms correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(5{,}000\text{ g}\) to \(\text{kg}\).
questions.explanation: Use the source-to-target unit conversion: \(\frac{5{,}000}{1{,}000}=5\text{ kg}\). The alternative \(50\text{ kg}\) divides by \(100\) instead of \(1{,}000\).
questions.hint: Identify the source and target units before choosing a scale factor.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a time given in hours to minutes correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(2\text{ h}\) to minutes.
questions.explanation: Use the source-to-target unit conversion: \(2\times 60=120\text{ min}\). The alternative \(100\text{ min}\) treats an hour as \(50\text{ min}\).
questions.hint: Time units use their own conversion relations.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a time given in minutes to hours correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(180\text{ min}\) to hours.
questions.explanation: Use the source-to-target unit conversion: \(\frac{180}{60}=3\text{ h}\). The alternative \(2\text{ h}\) would correspond to \(120\text{ min}\), not \(180\).
questions.hint: Identify the source and target units before choosing a scale factor.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a mass given in metric tons to kilograms correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(2.5\text{ t}\) to kilograms.
questions.explanation: Use the source-to-target unit conversion: \(2.5\times 1{,}000=2{,}500\text{ kg}\). The alternative \(250\text{ kg}\) uses \(100\text{ kg}\) per metric ton instead of \(1{,}000\).
questions.hint: Identify the source and target units before choosing a scale factor.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a time given in decimal hours to minutes correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(1.5\text{ h}\) to minutes.
questions.explanation: Use the source-to-target unit conversion: \(1.5\times 60=90\text{ min}\). The alternative \(150\text{ min}\) treats time as a base-ten conversion using \(100\text{ min}\) per hour.
questions.hint: Time units use their own conversion relations.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a time given in days to minutes correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(1\text{ day}\) to minutes.
questions.explanation: Use the source-to-target unit conversion: \(24\times 60=1{,}440\text{ min}\). The alternative \(2{,}400\text{ min}\) uses \(100\text{ min}\) per hour.
questions.hint: Identify the source and target units before choosing a scale factor.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a time given in seconds to hours correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(3{,}600\text{ s}\) to hours.
questions.explanation: Since \(1\text{ h}=60\times 60\text{ s}=3{,}600\text{ s}\), divide by \(3{,}600\): \(\frac{3{,}600}{3{,}600}=1\text{ h}\). The alternative \(2\text{ h}\) would require \(7{,}200\text{ s}\).
questions.hint: Time units use their own conversion relations.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a mass given in milligrams to grams correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(750\text{ mg}\) to \(\text{g}\).
questions.explanation: Use the source-to-target unit conversion: \(\frac{750}{1{,}000}=0.75\text{ g}\). The alternative \(7.5\text{ g}\) divides by \(100\) instead of \(1{,}000\).
questions.hint: Identify the source and target units before choosing a scale factor.

questions.concept: Mass Production Rate with Time Conversion
questions.learningObjective: Calculate total mass produced over a given time using unit conversion.
questions.question: A machine produces \(2.4\text{ kg}\) of material per minute. How many kilograms does it produce in \(1\text{ h}\)?
questions.explanation: Use the source-to-target unit conversion: \(2.4\times 60=144\text{ kg}\). The alternative \(24\text{ kg}\) uses a factor of \(10\) instead of the \(60\text{ min}\) in an hour.
questions.hint: Identify the source and target units before choosing a scale factor.
